report.summary: As of 2026-10-09 12:00 UTC, RR-001 is in planning: the only product document is a proposal, and no launch approval or customer exposure is evidenced. The stated target is 2026-10-16 10:00 UTC for a first cohort of 2,000 self-serve monthly Pro accounts. Four major planning decisions remain open: cancellation-completion behavior, reminder-toggle behavior, safe handling of conflicting billing evidence, and persistent cancellation status. Final training, content, CRM, staffing, vendor, and launch work is future preparation rather than a current readiness defect. For the stated launch target, the internal announcement deadline is 2026-10-13 10:00 UTC; actual send lead or lateness is not verified.

findings.finding: Approved cancellation-completion behavior remains unresolved. The proposal says the confirmation wording is under review, and Jo has not yet confirmed that billing acknowledgement must precede the success state or that loading must not claim completion.
findings.customer_consequence: If the eventual interface or agent guidance confirms cancellation before billing acknowledges it, customers may believe cancellation succeeded when it did not, creating access, renewal, and charge confusion.
findings.proposed_action: By 2026-10-10, approve and document the completion rule, including that success follows billing acknowledgement and that loading does not state cancellation is complete.

evidence.quote: Target launch: 2026-10-16 10:00 UTC. Reminder changes and cancellation-confirmation wording are under review; this is not approved behavior.

Inez proposes keeping the paid-access end date visible. Dev says billing acknowledgement must arrive before the success state; a loading state must not say the cancellation completed. Jo will confirm that requirement by Oct 10.

Product lead Jo approves customer behavior. Billing lead Sam approves refund and billing guidance. Engineering lead Dev supplies technical tests and fixes. Support readiness lead Mira recommends support readiness and rollout pauses. Release owner Jo authorizes launches and pauses. Engineering on-call Dev executes rollout changes. Vendor manager Lee confirms staffing and vendor access. Training owner Nia confirms training coverage; content owner Ren owns public and internal help; support operations owner Alex owns CRM and routing.

findings.finding: Whether this cohort honors an off renewal-reminder toggle remains an open product decision.
findings.customer_consequence: Customers may receive a reminder contrary to their selected setting, while agents may lack a consistent explanation of expected behavior.
findings.proposed_action: By 2026-10-10, approve whether an off reminder toggle is honored for the cohort and record the decision in the product behavior used for later content and training.

evidence.quote: Manage Plan will show a confirmation step, access end date and a success state after billing records cancellation. A planned email will restate the access end date. Refunds still require billing review and are never automatic. Renewal reminders currently run seven days before renewal when the customer's toggle is on.
Target launch: 2026-10-16 10:00 UTC. Reminder changes and cancellation-confirmation wording are under review; this is not approved behavior.

Open decisions: whether an off reminder toggle is honored in this cohort; what support should do if the account shows cancelled but billing evidence conflicts. Jo and Sam will decide both by Oct 10. No final training, staffing commitment or launch approval is expected at this planning meeting.

findings.finding: Safe support handling is unresolved for cases where the account shows cancelled but billing evidence conflicts.
findings.customer_consequence: Agents may give inconsistent cancellation or billing answers, fail to escalate the conflict, or imply a refund outcome without billing review.
findings.proposed_action: By 2026-10-10, approve safe agent steps and an escalation route for conflicting account and billing evidence, including a ban on promising automatic refunds, before exposure.

Cancellation and billing guidance must match the approved flow. Public content must be published for the exposed cohort. Every known billing issue needs safe guidance, an escalation route and the product owner's acceptance before exposure. Support launch readiness is not ready if this evidence is missing or contradicts the current behavior.

findings.finding: The proposal does not resolve Mira's contact-prevention request for a persistent account cancellation status; it specifies an access end date and success state but does not state that cancellation status remains visible.
findings.customer_consequence: Customers who leave the success screen may remain unable to verify cancellation later and may contact support about whether it completed.
findings.proposed_action: Decide whether completed cancellation status will remain visible in the account and, if accepted, add it to the approved flow before Ren and Nia prepare content and training; the decision due date is not supplied.

evidence.quote: Mira reports a recurring support theme: customers see an invoice after trying to cancel and cannot distinguish a completed cancellation from a click that failed. This is an illustrative support theme, not a measured ticket sample. She asks for a clear confirmation state and a persistent account status before suggesting more help content.

Product must send the internal announcement at least 72 hours before launch, naming the behavior revision and audience. Mira adapts it into a support notice. Internal and vendor agents need the current notice, training, internal guidance and access before serving exposed customers. Sending and acknowledgement are distinct. Vendor coverage requires a roster and a named lead's acknowledgement, including acknowledgement of late notice changes.

CRM contact reasons must be available on internal and vendor case forms, with old reasons mapped to new ones. Staffing requires stated volume assumptions, an AHT assumption (average handling time), reserve coverage and vendor acceptance. A planning estimate is not a demand forecast. If no infrastructure changes are needed, an owner can record a scoped no-change assessment rather than inventing work.
